system: You are an equity research assistant at a brokerage. Analysts use your summaries to decide quickly whether a news item matters for a specific stock. Accuracy matters more than completeness: never state anything the article does not support.
prompt:
Target stock: Apple (AAPL)

<article>
HEADLINE: Apple Intends to Expand Ads in App Store Search Results From 2026

BODY:
04:41 AM EST, 12/18/2025 (MT Newswires) -- Apple (AAPL) said Wednesday it plans to increase the number of advertisements that appear in its App Store search results from next year.

Apple Ads will introduce additional ads across search queries to help give advertisers "more opportunities" to drive downloads from search results, the iPhone maker said in an update posted on its website.

"If you have a search results campaign running, your ad will be automatically eligible for all available positions, but you can't select or bid for a particular one," the company said. "You'll be billed as usual based on your pricing model: cost per tap or cost per install."
</article>

Instructions:
1. Classify how relevant the article is to AAPL:
   - "primary": Apple is the main subject.
   - "secondary": Apple is one of several subjects, or a key driver of the story.
   - "peripheral": Apple is only mentioned in passing.
   - "none": Apple is not mentioned; any link would be your own inference.
2. Use only information stated in the article (headline + body). Do not add background knowledge,
   prices or context that is not in the text. If the body is missing or is generic boilerplate,
   rely on the headline and set "information_quality" to "limited".
3. Keep figures (prices, %, $ amounts, dates) exactly as written. Attribute analyst opinions,
   rumours and "sources say" reports as such.
4. Write for an investor in AAPL: the event, the key numbers, and why it could matter for the stock.
   If relevance is "peripheral" or "none", say so plainly and cover only what concerns AAPL
   (or, if nothing does, the market context in one sentence). Do not invent a connection.

Return only a JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "relevance": "primary" | "secondary" | "peripheral" | "none",
  "event_type": "earnings_guidance" | "analyst_action" | "m_and_a" | "regulatory_legal" | "product_business" | "macro_market" | "management_corporate" | "other",
  "summary": "<= 50 words, focused on AAPL",
  "key_facts": ["<= 3 short facts, each <= 15 words, keep figures"],
  "sentiment_for_ticker": "positive" | "negative" | "neutral" | "mixed",
  "sentiment_rationale": "<= 20 words",
  "information_quality": "full" | "limited"
}
